judgements.justification: In B, Ms3t's 3 rested partly on a wrong gSCAN validity claim and a wrong claim that no other technique was compared, and CnYk's 4 on a wrong reading of the parser as supervised; no A reviewer made these errors.
A's chair followed ratings of 6, 9, 6, 7 (mean 7.0) and its consensus statement is accurate; the spotlight is thinly argued but not set on the chair's own reading above the scores.
A's wEz8 gave 9 ('top 15%') after two hours in a review that is mostly summary with minor criticisms; it is the only rating in either committee that supports a spotlight.
The authors made the same concessions (hand-built world model, missing citations, misworded claims) to both committees.
The flaws A accepted are stated limitations and missing citations, weighed as minor (R08); stage 1 finds no substantive flaw in a result that A ignored.
The rebuttal moved oMsG up to 6 in A, while no score moved in B, though Ms3t received the same framing and human-study explanation.
Only B raised the unreported inference cost (jmVT) and the unmeasured parser errors in CLUTRR (2tE8), both correct, and B's meta-review lists them among its concerns.
Both committees saw the hand-designed world model; A's Tn5q and Eow4 accepted it as a stated limitation of a proof of concept, while B's meta-review named it the main reason to reject.
Neither chair adopted one reviewer's position over split reviews; both followed unanimous ratings.
No reviewer in either committee is recorded as moving because of the other reviews.
The authors answered every reviewer in both committees; Ms3t's silence is the reviewer's, not a missed reply.
wEz8's 9 at confidence 5 rested on summary and praise, wEz8 never replied to the rebuttal or joined the discussion, and the score counted unchallenged toward A's spotlight.
B's chair rejected with all four ratings below threshold (5, 4, 3, 5).
B's chair stated no positive assessment of its own; 'close but just below the bar' follows unanimous below-threshold scores.
B's low scores rest on the world model, novelty and misreadings, which are central claims, not peripheral variants the method does not use.
Both committees evaluated the paper as a neuro-symbolic generation method; they differed in the bar for generality, not in the kind of contribution.
oMsG, who moved in A, did not say the core was outside his expertise; the move rested on explanation, which R06 covers.

Both read the paper as a method; B required a general way to build the world model and tests beyond simple domains, while A, through Tn5q and Eow4, accepted a proof of concept for a narrow world model.
No praise in either committee rests on a wrong factual claim; Tn5q's wrong budget of 20 is a question, not a basis for praise.

added.name: Reviewer kept score after main concern answered
added.definition: A reviewer in one committee acknowledged that the rebuttal resolved the concern their score rested on, yet kept the same below-threshold score by citing new or secondary grounds, so the correction did not change the committee's ratings.
added.justification: R01 covers the wrong claim itself and R15 a score held on a peripheral point the authors had answered; neither covers a reviewer who conceded that the main concern was answered and then kept the score on new grounds.

reasoning: The core cause is R08 with R18: both committees saw the hand-designed world model, and A accepted it as a stated limit of a proof of concept while B required generality. A's spotlight rests on wEz8's thin, unengaged 9 (R03, R12). The rebuttal moved A's main critic but no B reviewer (R06). B's low scores rest partly on wrong claims (R01), and one B reviewer conceded his main concern was answered yet kept 4 on new grounds, which no existing reason names, so R20 is added. B also raised correct secondary issues A did not (R07).
